standard.title: Recognise and respond to classroom language
standard.description: recognise and respond to modelled classroom-related greetings, instructions and routines, and personal introductions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can recognise meaning and communicate using modelled words, gestures and formulaic phrases with support (AC9LSF01). They have no formal curriculum experience with structured classroom routines, following instructions, or producing personal introductions in the target language.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise and respond to modelled greetings, classroom instructions, routines and personal introductions in the target language, and use modelled language to introduce themselves and express simple personal information.

nodes.label: Recognising and responding to greetings and farewells
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and respond appropriately to modelled greetings and farewells — selecting responses appropriate to time of day, relationship and context.
nodes.minimum_width: Respond correctly to at least three different greeting and farewell exchanges using appropriate target language or action.
nodes.typical_width: Participate in greetings and farewells across varied time-of-day and relationship contexts; use formulaic expressions for thanks, apologies, praise and well wishes; recognise and use expressions for special occasions.
wider: Initiate a greeting independently using the appropriate contextual form without teacher prompting
Explain to a peer or family member the meaning of two or three greeting expressions and when they are used
nodes.hinge_reason: Greeting and farewell routines are the daily entry point for all classroom target language use. Students who cannot manage these exchanges are excluded from the social fabric of the language classroom and cannot engage with instruction or personal introduction work.

response_modes.reason: Greeting and farewell language becomes automatic only through daily repetition in real routine contexts — the routine itself is the practice vehicle.

success_criteria: Responds correctly to at least three different greeting or farewell exchanges using appropriate target language or action
Uses at least two formulaic expressions (thanks, apology, praise) correctly in context

nodes.label: Following classroom instructions and routines
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can follow and respond to modelled classroom instructions, commands and routine language — using action, gesture or target language response.
nodes.minimum_width: Respond correctly to at least four different classroom commands or instructions using appropriate action or target language.
nodes.typical_width: Follow and respond to a range of classroom commands, activity instructions and routine exchanges (roll call, weather, day and date); respond to instructions for creative and physical activities; use target language for simple classroom requests.
wider: Follow a sequence of three or more instructions in the target language without repetition — demonstrating processing of connected instruction sets
Give a simple instruction to a partner in the target language and check that it was understood

response_modes.reason: Instruction-following accuracy requires daily repetition in real classroom contexts. The classroom routine itself is the practice vehicle.

success_criteria: Follows at least four different classroom commands correctly using action or target language response
Responds to a classroom request or routine question using appropriate target language

nodes.label: Producing personal introductions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can produce personal introductions and respond to simple personal questions using modelled sentence structures — including personal details and expressions of preference.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce a personal introduction with at least three elements using modelled sentence structures.
nodes.typical_width: Use modelled sentence structures to introduce themselves with name, age, family members, and preferences; ask and respond to simple personal questions; use visual supports such as photos and props.
wider: Produce an extended self-introduction adding at least two personal details beyond the modelled minimum — using adapted rather than verbatim language
Ask a partner at least two personal questions and respond to two questions in a short unrehearsed exchange

response_modes.reason: Personal introduction language requires a bank of sentence frames across personal domains. Students need exposure to varied frame types before they can adapt them for genuine personal expression.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Personal introduction is the first genuinely communicative task — students share real information about themselves. Width investment here produces authentic language use and establishes the pattern of using the target language for genuine personal expression.
success_criteria: Produces a personal introduction with at least three elements using modelled sentence structures
Responds correctly to at least two simple personal questions
